cmadmin: Somewhere right now there is someone who knows general insurance inside out, and still spends the day retyping what the record already holds.
You retype the proposal form. You wait three days for an endorsement. And the history you are advising on sits in four different places.
The branch has opened its own general insurance agency. And it already has a book.
You would not be building a book. We have one. A hundred and three clients, a hundred and ninety five policies in force, and renewals in every single month of the year.
Before you open a file, every term since the policy began is already on the screen. What was covered, at what value, what was paid, and the claims that fell in each term.
The insurer's notice is read for you, and every figure is checked against our own record. Where the two disagree, the desk says so.
The job is the part a system cannot do. Endorsements and extensions. The renewal conversation. Telling a client plainly what the cover does and what it does not. And knowing when the Act changes.
Here is the part most people in this work never get. A change you ask for is not a ticket in a queue at head office. It is written into the desk, and it runs on every file that week.
A renewal that goes out thirty days ahead with the claims history on it. An endorsement nobody has to retype. A flag when a sum insured has not moved in three years.
The paperwork is finished. The advice is not. That is the job.
One seat, for a client manager. Chaguanas. Come and look after the book.
